title: Bees Make Better Dads Than We Thought - Nautilus

text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyBees Make Better Dads Than We ThoughtSo much for “flying bags of sperm”JCBy Jake Currie2:00 PM CST on November 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWhat are male bumblebees even for? Powered By 10 ShareNextStayQueen bees control the fertilization of their eggs with diploid females becoming workers who gather food and the cheaper-to-produce haploid males becoming drones. Traditionally, these males were thought to only contribute the genetic material necessary to kickstart a new colony, earning them the dismissive nickname “flying sperm bags.” But now a new study published in Royal Society Open Science suggests they may be much more important. Prior to this study, just one other investigation (by Sydney Cameron, now at the University of Illinois), probed the role males play in bumblebee colonies and found they shared in the brood care of their siblings. It piqued the curiosity of a team of entomologists from the University of California, Riverside, so they snapped some thermal photos of bumblebee nests. The images showed males poised over the brood in an “incubation posture.” This allows them to make contact with eggs while they work their muscles, generating heat.   Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
